mainTopic: מלקות for cooking or eating חלב in milk, and which animals' milk is included in the איסור of בשר בחלב.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the argument between רבי אמי and רבי אסי about מלקות for cooking or eating חלב in milk. It gives three versions: no lashes for eating with an argument about cooking; lashes for cooking with an argument about eating; or no argument at all. A ברייתא then challenges the view of אין איסור חל על איסור, since it says פיגול, נותר and טמא meat cooked in milk does bring lashes. The גמרא answers that this ברייתא follows a תנא who holds איסור חל על איסור. The same ברייתא's ruling that cooking in whey is פטור is shown to support ריש לקיש. Next, two ברייתות use the repeated words בחלב אמו to include cow and ewe milk and the milk of the kid's older sister, and each time רב אשי explains why a קל וחומר from the mother is not enough. The younger sister is learned through a הצד השוה of the mother and the older sister. Finally the גמרא agrees that the older sister can be learned this way too, so the extra בחלב אמו must teach something else, and a ברייתא explaining this begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No lashes for eating means no lashes for cooking
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the first version of the argument. It gives the reason of the one who says there is no מלקות for cooking חלב in milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since a person is not flogged for eating it, he is also not flogged for cooking it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining the view that cooking חלב in milk brings no מלקות. Eating and cooking are tied together, so if eating brings no lashes, cooking brings none either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this first version, everyone agrees there is no מלקות for eating חלב cooked in milk, because of אין איסור חל על איסור. The Torah expresses the eating prohibition with the words of cooking (לא תבשל), so the two go together. That is why the lack of מלקות for eating carries over to cooking.

keyTerms.meaning: He is flogged (receives מלקות)
Eating
Cooking
Also

phrases.english: Since for eating he is not flogged,
phrases.notes: This is talking about חלב, the forbidden fat, cooked in milk. Everyone already agreed there are no lashes for eating it.

phrases.english: for cooking he is also not flogged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reasoning of the first version, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the first version, the one who says no מלקות holds that because eating brings no lashes, cooking brings none either.

steps.title: Second version: everyone agrees about cooking, and the argument is about eating
steps.stepSummary: An alternate report of the מחלוקת flips it around. Everyone agrees there is מלקות for cooking, and the argument is only about eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: about cooking, everyone agrees he is flogged. Where they argue is about eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of what רבי אמי and רבי אסי were arguing about. This sets up the next step, which explains each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, eating was agreed upon and cooking was argued about. Here it is the opposite: cooking clearly brings מלקות, and eating is the open question. The reason cooking is clear is that אין איסור חל על איסור does not apply to cooking, since cooking חלב was never forbidden on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone (both sides) agrees
They argue

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the versions. Version one: eating is agreed (no מלקות), cooking is argued. Version two: cooking is agreed (מלקות), eating is argued.

phrases.english: And some say:

phrases.aramaic: אַבִּישּׁוּל – כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּלָקֵי,
phrases.english: about cooking, everyone agrees that he is flogged,
where they argue is about eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of the argument that step 1 finished explaining.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cooking חלב in milk brings מלקות according to everyone. The argument is only about eating it.

steps.title: Each side's reason in the second version
steps.stepSummary: The no-lashes side uses אין איסור חל על איסור. The lashes side says the Torah wrote eating in the language of cooking to link them, so lashes for cooking means lashes for eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says he is not flogged reasons that a prohibition cannot take effect on another prohibition. The one who says he is flogged says this is exactly why the Torah wrote eating in the language of cooking: since he is flogged for cooking, he is also flogged for eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind each side of the argument about eating in the second version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The no-lashes side says the fat was already forbidden as חלב, so the meat-and-milk prohibition cannot add to it. The lashes side uses the same link from step 1, but in the other direction. Here cooking definitely brings lashes, so eating does too. The link between eating and cooking is strong enough to get past the rule of אין איסור חל על איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: A new prohibition cannot take effect on something that is already forbidden
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳
He expressed it (literally, 'brought it out')
In the language of

steps.whyThisMatters: The same link between eating and cooking is used in both versions, but it gives opposite results depending on which act is the agreed starting point.

phrases.english: The one who says he is not flogged

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא אֵין אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר,
phrases.english: because a prohibition does not take effect on a prohibition;
and the one who says he is flogged
for this reason the Merciful One expressed
eating in the language of cooking,
phrases.notes: The Torah says 'לא תבשל' (do not cook), and one of those times is understood to forbid eating too.

phrases.english: since for cooking he is flogged,
for eating he is also flogged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two sides of the second version introduced in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No-lashes side: אין איסור חל על איסור. Lashes side: the Torah links eating to cooking, so lashes for cooking means lashes for eating.

steps.title: Third version: they do not really argue
steps.stepSummary: A third approach says each אמורא spoke about a different act, so there is no real argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: one Sage said one thing and the other Sage said another, and they do not argue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that רבי אמי and רבי אסי are not arguing at all. One was speaking about cooking (lashes) and the other about eating (no lashes).
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, both agree to אין איסור חל על איסור, so there is no מלקות for eating חלב in milk. Both also agree there is מלקות for cooking it. Their statements only looked like they disagreed because each was talking about a different act.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: introduces another possible explanation

keyTerms.term: מָר אֲמַר חֲדָא וּמָר אֲמַר חֲדָא
keyTerms.meaning: One Sage said one thing and the other said another: they were discussing different cases

steps.whatToRemember: Three versions: (1) no lashes for eating, and they argue about cooking; (2) lashes for cooking, and they argue about eating; (3) no argument at all: lashes for cooking, no lashes for eating.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: מָר אֲמַר חֲדָא, וּמָר אֲמַר חֲדָא,
phrases.english: one Sage said one thing, and one Sage said another thing,
phrases.notes: The lashes statement was about cooking, and the no-lashes statement was about eating.

phrases.english: and they do not argue.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: מָר אֲמַר חֲדָא, וּמָר אֲמַר חֲדָא, וְלָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third way to understand the two statements, removing the argument altogether.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is מלקות for cooking חלב in milk but not for eating it, and both אמוראים agree.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists cases of cooking in milk that are exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge one of the views. It starts with cases where cooking in milk is פטור: whey, blood, bones, tendons, horns and hooves.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: one who cooks in whey is exempt. Blood that he cooked in milk is exempt. Bones, tendons, horns and hooves that he cooked in milk are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge by quoting a ברייתא about cooking in milk. The punchline of the challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case is פטור because something is missing. Whey is not counted as real milk, and blood, bones, tendons, horns and hooves are not counted as meat. These cases lay the groundwork for the attack on the views just presented.

keyTerms.meaning: Whey, the liquid left after milk curdles
Exempt (no punishment)
Tendons or sinews
Hooves

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
one who cooks in whey is exempt,
blood that he cooked in milk, he is exempt,
the bones and the tendons
and the horns and the hooves
that he cooked in milk, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge from a ברייתא against the positions laid out in steps 1-4.
steps.kashyaTarget: One of the positions about מלקות for cooking or eating חלב in milk. Step 6 shows that the target is the view of אין איסור חל על איסור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists cases of cooking in milk and says which are exempt. Its rulings will be compared against the views of רבי אמי and רבי אסי.

steps.title: Forbidden sacrificial meat cooked in milk is liable
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by ruling that פיגול, נותר and טמא meat cooked in milk brings lashes. This is the punchline of the challenge against the view of אין איסור חל על איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: But פיגול, נותר, and טמא meat that someone cooked in milk: he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the previous step finishes. It says that someone who cooks already-forbidden קדשים meat in milk does get lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פיגול, נותר and טמא meat are already forbidden to eat. If cooking them in milk still brings lashes, then the איסור of בשר בחלב took effect on top of an existing איסור. That goes against the view that said אין איסור חל על איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: A קרבן that became forbidden because it was offered with the intent to eat it or sprinkle its blood after its proper time
Meat of a קרבן left over after the time allowed for eating it
Here: קרבן meat that became ritually impure and so may not be eaten
Liable, here meaning he gets lashes

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new ruling standing by itself. It is the end of the ברייתא brought in step 5, and it is the part that actually creates the challenge.

phrases.english: Piggul, notar, and impure meat,
phrases.notes: All three are kinds of קרבן meat that are already forbidden to eat.

phrases.english: that one cooked in milk: he is liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַפִּגּוּל, וְהַנּוֹתָר, וְהַטָּמֵא, שֶׁבִּשְּׁלָן בְּחָלָב – חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 5 and delivers the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that there are no lashes because אין איסור חל על איסור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Meat that is already forbidden still gets lashes for cooking in milk, which shows that the second איסור does take effect on top of the first.

steps.title: This תנא holds a prohibition takes effect on a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows a תנא who holds איסור חל על איסור. The אמוראים who disagree follow the other side of a known מחלוקת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תנא holds that an איסור takes effect on top of another איסור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the ברייתא only reflects one opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether איסור חל על איסור is already a known מחלוקת among תנאים. So a ברייתא that holds it does take effect does not disprove the אמוראים. They simply follow the תנאים who say it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: A second prohibition takes effect on something that is already forbidden
A sage of the משנה period, whose opinion is recorded in a ברייתא

phrases.english: This tanna holds
that a prohibition takes effect on a prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The ruling depends on a known מחלוקת among the תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to disprove the view of אין איסור חל על איסור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows one side of the מחלוקת. The אמוראים follow the other side.

steps.title: Whey ruling supports ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's ruling that cooking in whey is פטור supports ריש לקיש. He said the משנה treating whey like milk applies only to making produce able to become טמא, not to בשר בחלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said one who cooks in whey is exempt. This supports ריש לקיש, because a משנה teaches: whey is like milk, and olive liquid is like oil. ריש לקיש said: they taught this only for making seeds able to become impure. But for cooking meat in milk, whey is not like milk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first case of the ברייתא, whey, and shows that it supports ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה says whey counts as milk, so you might think it counts as milk for בשר בחלב too. ריש לקיש limited that משנה to the laws of הכשר, making food able to become טמא. The ברייתא says cooking meat in whey is פטור, which matches him exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Whey, the watery liquid left after milk is curdled
The liquid that seeps out of olives
To make food able to become טמא through contact with certain liquids
It supports him
Exempt, here meaning no lashes

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the same thing can count as milk for one area of הלכה and not for another.

phrases.english: One who cooks in whey is exempt,
phrases.notes: This is quoting the first case of the ברייתא from step 5.

phrases.english: this supports Reish Lakish,

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: מֵי חָלָב הֲרֵי הֵן כְּחָלָב,
phrases.english: as we learned: whey is like milk,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in מכשירין 6:5, about liquids that make food able to become טמא.

phrases.english: and olive secretion is like oil.
Reish Lakish said: they taught this
only for making seeds susceptible to impurity,
but regarding cooking meat in milk,
whey is not like milk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the first case of the ברייתא from step 5 and uses it as support for an אמורא.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's rule that whey is not milk for בשר בחלב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's ruling that one who cooks meat in whey is פטור

steps.title: Source that any animal's milk is included
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא asks: the פסוק says 'in its mother's milk', so where do we learn that the milk of a cow or a sheep is also included?
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'in its mother's milk' - from this I only know about the mother's own milk. How do I know that the milk of a cow or a ewe is included?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that asks for a source. It is setting up the answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, the פסוק forbids only a kid in its own mother's milk. The ברייתא assumes any milk is forbidden and asks which words of the Torah teach this.

keyTerms.meaning: "In its mother's milk", the words of the פסוק forbidding בשר בחלב
"I only have...", meaning the פסוק by itself teaches only this case
From where do we learn it?

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not mean that only mother's milk is forbidden. It is asking where the Torah teaches that other milk is included too.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: "In its mother's milk":
I have only its mother's milk;
from where do I know the milk of a cow and a ewe?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the source for widening the milk in the איסור.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which words of the פסוק include milk from animals other than the mother

steps.title: A קל וחומר to include cow and ewe milk, and then a פסוק anyway
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a קל וחומר: if a mother goat, which may mate with the kid, is still forbidden for cooking with it, then a cow or ewe, which may not mate with it, should surely be forbidden. Still, it ends by bringing the פסוק 'בחלב אמו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: You could argue a קל וחומר: the kid's own mother may mate with it, and still she is forbidden to be cooked with it. A cow and a ewe may not mate with it, so surely they are forbidden to be cooked with it! That is why the פסוק says 'בחלב אמו'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from step 9 about cow and sheep milk. It offers a logical argument, but then still brings the פסוק 'בחלב אמו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is that the mother is 'closer' to the kid, since mating between them is allowed, yet cooking them together is still forbidden. A cow or ewe is 'farther' from the kid, since mating is forbidden, so cooking should be forbidden even more. Strangely, the ברייתא then adds a פסוק anyway, and that sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stricter case: if the light case has a rule, the strict case surely does
Mating animals together
Isn't it logical? (the conclusion of a קל וחומר)
Therefore the פסוק says (bringing a source from the Torah)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the mother is the 'strict' side here. In this קל וחומר, the mother is the lighter case, since mating with her is allowed, and the cow and ewe are the stricter case.

phrases.english: You can say an a fortiori argument:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה אִמּוֹ, שֶׁלֹּא נֶאֶסְרָה עִמּוֹ בְּהַרְבָּעָה –
phrases.english: Just as its mother, which is not forbidden with it for mating,
is forbidden with it for cooking,
a cow and a ewe, which are forbidden with it for mating,
isn't it logical that they are forbidden with it for cooking!
Therefore the verse says: "In its mother's milk."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question from step 9 about including the milk of a cow or ewe.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Cow and ewe milk is included, first by a קל וחומר from the mother, and then by a repeated 'בחלב אמו'.

steps.title: Why a פסוק if the קל וחומר already works?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: if the קל וחומר already teaches that cow and ewe milk is forbidden, why bring a פסוק?
steps.simpleTranslation: But why do I need a פסוק? We already learned it from the קל וחומר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא for bringing a פסוק to teach something the קל וחומר already proved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not need to write something we can figure out by logic. So if the קל וחומר is solid, the extra 'בחלב אמו' looks wasted. Either the פסוק is extra, or the קל וחומר has a weakness.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need a פסוק? (asked when logic already teaches the point)
It comes, meaning it is already learned (from the logic)

phrases.english: But why do I need a verse?
It was already derived for him!
phrases.notes: He means the קל וחומר in the ברייתא already taught this.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא לְמָה לִי קְרָא? הָא אָתְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's use of a פסוק right after its קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's bringing of 'בחלב אמו' to include cow and ewe milk
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a קל וחומר already proves the rule, a פסוק teaching the same rule is not needed.

steps.title: The קל וחומר can be refuted, so the פסוק is needed
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the קל וחומר has a weakness at its base. The mother is stricter in one way: she may not be slaughtered on the same day as her young, while a cow may be. So the פסוק is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Because one can say the argument is broken from the start. Where are you learning from? From its mother. But the mother is special, because she is forbidden to be slaughtered with it. Can you say the same about a cow, which is not forbidden to be slaughtered with it? That is why the פסוק says 'בחלב אמו'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers step 11's challenge by showing that the קל וחומר can be broken. Since the logic is weak, the ברייתא needs the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the source case is lighter in every way. Here the mother is lighter in mating, but stricter in slaughter, because of the rule of אותו ואת בנו. Because the mother has her own strict side, we cannot be sure the cow is stricter overall, so the פסוק must teach it.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation that knocks down a logical argument
From the very base of the argument
Slaughtering an animal
The ban on slaughtering an animal and its young on the same day

steps.whatToRemember: A קל וחומר fails if the 'lighter' case turns out to be stricter in some other way. Here the mother is stricter in slaughter, so cow and ewe milk is learned from the פסוק, not from logic.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Because one can say
there is a refutation from the very base of the argument:
From where are you bringing it? From its mother.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְאִמּוֹ שֶׁכֵּן נֶאֶסְרָה עִמּוֹ בִּשְׁחִיטָה,
phrases.english: What about its mother? She is special, since she is forbidden with it for slaughter.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:28: you may not slaughter a mother and its young on the same day.

phrases.aramaic: תֹּאמַר בְּפָרָה שֶׁלֹּא נֶאֶסְרָה עִמּוֹ בִּשְׁחִיטָה?
phrases.english: Will you say the same about a cow, which is not forbidden with it for slaughter?
Therefore the verse says: "In its mother's milk."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מִשּׁוּם דְּאִיכָּא לְמֵימַר מֵעִיקָּרָא דְּדִינָא פִּירְכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by refuting the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refuting the logical argument (פירכא), which shows the פסוק is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר alone proves cow and ewe milk is forbidden, so the פסוק is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קל וחומר is broken because the mother is stricter in slaughter, so the פסוק is the real source.

steps.title: A new ברייתא: what about the milk of an older sister?
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says that 'בחלב אמו' alone teaches only the mother's milk. It asks where we learn that the milk of the kid's older sister is also included.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: 'בחלב אמו' teaches me only its mother's milk. From where do I learn its older sister's milk?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that starts a new question about the third mention of 'בחלב אמו'. It is setting up an answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 10 to 12 used the phrase to include cow and ewe milk. Now a new ברייתא asks about another animal of the same species that is not the mother, the kid's older sister. The question widens who counts as 'its mother' for this איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: I would only know (this narrow case from the פסוק)
Its older sister
From where do we learn it?

phrases.english: It is taught in another baraita:

phrases.aramaic: ״בַּחֲלֵב אִמּוֹ״ – אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בַּחֲלֵב אִמּוֹ,
phrases.english: "In its mother's milk": I have only the milk of its mother.
From where do I know the milk of its older sister?

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ: ״בַּחֲלֵב אִמּוֹ״ – אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בַּחֲלֵב אִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the finished cow-and-ewe question to a new ברייתא about the third 'בחלב אמו'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for forbidding meat cooked in the milk of the kid's older sister.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from the mother to the older sister
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a קל וחומר: the mother, which enters the tithing pen with the kid, is forbidden with it for cooking. So the sister, which does not enter the pen with it, should surely be forbidden. Still, it ends by quoting the פסוק 'בחלב אמו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: You could say a קל וחומר: the mother enters the pen with the kid to be tithed, and she is still forbidden to be cooked with it. The sister does not enter the pen with it to be tithed. Isn't it logical that she is forbidden for cooking with it? So the פסוק says 'בחלב אמו'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from step 13 with a קל וחומר from the mother to the older sister, and then also quotes the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother has a closer connection to the kid in one way: she can go into the tithing pen together with it. Even so, she is forbidden with it for cooking. The older sister has less of a connection, so it seems obvious she should be forbidden too. Ending with a פסוק, after a קל וחומר seems to have already done the job, sets up the גמרא's next question.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument: if the lighter case has a rule, the heavier case surely has it too
Pen or enclosure for animals
To be tithed, meaning the animal-tithing count
Isn't it logical?
The פסוק teaches

phrases.english: You can say a kal vachomer:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה אִמּוֹ שֶׁנִּכְנְסָה עִמּוֹ לְדִיר לְהִתְעַשֵּׂר –
phrases.english: Just as its mother, which enters the pen with it to be tithed,
phrases.notes: For the animal tithe, animals were counted as they passed out of a pen. The mother can be counted together with this kid.

phrases.english: is forbidden for cooking with it,

phrases.aramaic: אֲחוֹתוֹ שֶׁלֹּא נִכְנְסָה עִמּוֹ לְדִיר לְהִתְעַשֵּׂר –
phrases.english: its sister, which does not enter the pen with it to be tithed,
is it not logical that she is forbidden for cooking with it!
The verse says: 'In its mother's milk.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13, following the same pattern as step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from the mother, and then the פסוק 'בחלב אמו'

steps.title: Why is a פסוק needed for the sister?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the קל וחומר already teaches the sister, why bring a פסוק?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need a פסוק? It was already learned from the קל וחומר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא for bringing a פסוק when its own logic already seemed enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of challenge as step 11. A פסוק should not be used up on something we could know through logic alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need a פסוק?
It comes, meaning it can be learned

phrases.english: But why do I need a verse?
It was already derived for him!
phrases.notes: "It" means the rule about the sister. The ברייתא already got it from the קל וחומר.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא לְמָה לִי קְרָא, הָא אָתְיָא לַיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's use of a פסוק in step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's quoting of 'בחלב אמו' for the older sister
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק is unnecessary when a קל וחומר already proves the rule

steps.title: רב אשי: the קל וחומר can be knocked down
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the קל וחומר is weak from its base. The mother is stricter because she is forbidden to be slaughtered with her young on the same day, and the older sister is not. So a פסוק is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: because you can attack the argument at its base. Where are you learning it from? From the mother. But the mother is special, since she is forbidden with it for slaughtering. Can you say the same about the older sister, who is not forbidden with it for slaughtering? That is why the פסוק says 'בחלב אמו'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge. The קל וחומר does not really hold up, so the פסוק is needed after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the source case is lighter in every relevant way. The mother is stricter in one area, the same-day slaughter rule, so maybe that is why she is forbidden in cooking too. The older sister lacks that strictness, so logic alone cannot include her.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation that knocks down an argument
From the very base of the argument
Slaughtering
Will you say? This is how a weakness in a comparison is pointed out

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a קל וחומר from the mother alone fails for any animal that lacks her special strictness of same-day slaughter. Steps 22-23 later show that the older sister can still be learned by combining the mother with a cow.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Because one can say
there is a refutation at the base of the argument:
From where are you bringing it?
From its mother.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְאִמּוֹ, שֶׁכֵּן נֶאֶסְרָה עִמּוֹ בִּשְׁחִיטָה,
phrases.english: What about its mother? She is special because she is forbidden with it for slaughter.
Will you say the same about its older sister,
who is not forbidden with it for slaughter?
Therefore the verse says: 'In its mother's milk.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מִשּׁוּם דְּאִיכָּא לְמֵימַר מֵעִיקָּרָא דְּדִינָא פִּירְכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 in the same way as step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a weakness (פירכא) in the קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר alone proves the older sister is forbidden
steps.terutzMaskana: The mother is stricter because of the same-day slaughter rule, so the פסוק is needed to include the older sister

steps.title: What about the younger sister?
steps.stepSummary: Now we have a source for the older sister. The גמרא asks where we learn that the younger sister's milk is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for the older sister. Where do we learn the younger sister?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new case, the kid's younger sister, and asks for her source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The older sister is covered by the פסוק, but the younger sister is a different case. The גמרא needs to show how she is included.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found
Its younger sister
From where do we learn it?

phrases.english: We have found a source for its older sister;
from where do we know its younger sister?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן אֲחוֹתוֹ גְּדוֹלָה, אֲחוֹתוֹ קְטַנָּה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the source for the older sister and asks about a further case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the younger sister's milk is included

steps.title: Learned from the two cases together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the younger sister is learned from between the two cases, the mother and the older sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes from between them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short answer: the younger sister is learned by combining the mother and the older sister. The next steps will explain how.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither case alone is strong enough. Together they make a combined proof, where each case covers the other's weak point.

keyTerms.meaning: From between them, meaning from the two cases together
The common factor: learning from what two cases share

phrases.english: It is derived from between them.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the mother and the older sister, the two cases we already have.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The younger sister is learned from the mother and the older sister combined

steps.title: Why can't we learn from the mother alone?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which case the younger sister should be learned from. If from the mother alone, there is a weakness: the mother is forbidden with the kid for שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From which case should it come? If it comes from the mother, you can say the mother is special, since she is forbidden with it for slaughtering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining why both cases are needed. It shows that the mother alone is not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The younger sister, like the older sister, is not part of the same-day slaughter rule. So the mother's special strictness blocks learning the younger sister from the mother alone.

keyTerms.meaning: From which case should it come?
What about this case? It is special because... This is the standard way to point out a weakness.

phrases.english: From which should it be derived?
Should it be derived from its mother?

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְאִמּוֹ שֶׁכֵּן נֶאֶסְרָה עִמּוֹ בִּשְׁחִיטָה?
phrases.english: What about its mother? She is special because she is forbidden with it for slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the short answer of step 18
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which source the younger sister is learned from, given that the mother alone has a weakness

steps.title: Each case covers the other's weakness
steps.stepSummary: The older sister proves that the slaughter rule does not matter, since she is not part of it and is still forbidden. If someone says the older sister is special because she does not enter the tithing pen, the mother proves that does not matter either. So the younger sister is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: The older sister proves it. But what about the older sister? She does not enter the pen with it to be tithed. The mother proves it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the combined proof. Each case answers the weakness of the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother's special feature (the slaughter rule) is answered by the older sister, who does not have that feature and is still forbidden. The older sister's special feature (not entering the pen) is answered by the mother, who does enter the pen and is still forbidden. Since neither feature is the real reason, what the two cases share applies to the younger sister too.

keyTerms.meaning: Will prove: this case shows that the claimed weakness does not matter
Its older sister

steps.whatToRemember: The mother's milk comes straight from the פסוק. A קל וחומר from the mother alone can be knocked down, because of her special strictness in slaughter. The younger sister is learned from the mother and the older sister together, since each covers the other's weakness. Steps 22-23 then show that the older sister can be learned the same way, from the mother and a cow.

phrases.english: Its older sister proves it.
What about its older sister?
She is special because she does not enter the pen with it to be tithed.
Its mother proves it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the combined proof started in step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each source cancels the other's weakness, so the younger sister is included through what the two cases share

steps.title: The common element includes the younger sister
steps.stepSummary: The mother and the older sister each have a weakness the other does not share. Their common element is that both are meat and may not be cooked in milk. So the younger sister, which is also meat, is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the reasoning comes back around. This case is not like that case, and that case is not like this case. What they share is that each is meat and may not be cooked in milk. So I will also include the younger sister, because she is meat and may not be cooked in milk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up its proof from Step 20. It uses a הצד השוה to show that the younger sister's milk is also forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source had a weak point. The mother has the ban on slaughtering with her young, and the older sister has the fact that she does not enter the tithing pen. Since neither weakness is found in both, only the shared feature counts: both are meat and both are forbidden to cook in milk. The younger sister has that shared feature, so she is included.

keyTerms.meaning: The reasoning has come back around (to the starting point)
This case is not like that case; each source has its own special feature
The common element shared by both sources
Its younger sister

steps.whatToRemember: A הצד השוה works by ignoring each source's special feature and building only on what both sources share.

phrases.english: And the reasoning has come back around:
the aspect of this case is not like the aspect of that one,
phrases.notes: "This" and "that" are the mother and the older sister.

phrases.english: and the aspect of that case is not like the aspect of this one;
the common element between them is
that it is meat and it is forbidden to cook it in milk.
So I too will include its younger sister,
since it is meat, and it is forbidden to cook it in milk.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזַר הַדִּין, לֹא רְאִי זֶה כִּרְאִי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the הצד השוה argument begun in Step 20 and states its result.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The younger sister is included in the ban on cooking in milk through the shared feature of the mother and the older sister.

steps.title: Then the older sister should also be learned from a common element
steps.stepSummary: If a הצד השוה works here, then the older sister could also be learned from a combination of two sources. In that case, she would not need a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the older sister should also be learned from between two sources.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the earlier claim in Step 16 that the older sister needs a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 16, the older sister needed a פסוק because the קל וחומר from the mother alone was weak. But the same method just used for the younger sister could also work for the older sister by combining the mother with another source, a cow. Each of those has its own stringency, but they share being meat that may not be cooked in milk. If that works, the פסוק for the older sister seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your reasoning is right)
Its older sister
Let it be learned from between them, by combining two sources

phrases.english: If so,
let its older sister also be learned from between them.
phrases.notes: Here "them" means the mother and a cow. Each has its own stringency, but they share being meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֲחוֹתוֹ גְּדוֹלָה נָמֵי תֵּיתֵי מִבֵּינַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the method that just succeeded and turns it against the earlier need for a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 16's claim that a פסוק is needed for the older sister
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A הצד השוה from two sources can include the older sister, so the פסוק looks extra.

steps.title: The גמרא agrees, so why is the פסוק needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that the older sister can be learned through a הצד השוה. This raises a new question: what are the words ״בַּחֲלֵב אִמּוֹ״ teaching?
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. But then why do I need the words "in its mother's milk"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees with the challenge instead of rejecting it. It then sets up the next move by asking what job the פסוק now has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא accepts the objection: the older sister really can be learned through the הצד השוה. But a פסוק never says extra words for no reason. So the words ״בַּחֲלֵב אִמּוֹ״ must teach something else, and the גמרא now has to find out what.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so (the גמרא agrees with the challenge)
Why do I need it?
In its mother's milk (words from the פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: ״אִין הָכִי נָמֵי״ is not a rejection. The גמרא is agreeing, and that agreement is what forces the new question about the פסוק.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so.
But then why do I need "in its mother's milk"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי, אֶלָּא בַּחֲלֵב אִמּוֹ לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts Step 22's challenge and turns it into a question about what the פסוק teaches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concession: the challenge is accepted, and the פסוק is given a new purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words ״בַּחֲלֵב אִמּוֹ״ were needed to include the older sister.
steps.terutzMaskana: The older sister comes from the הצד השוה, so the פסוק must teach something else.

steps.title: The פסוק is needed for a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The words ״בַּחֲלֵב אִמּוֹ״ are needed for a lesson taught in a ברייתא. The ברייתא begins by saying that, from these words alone, we would only know about the mother's milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for what is taught in a ברייתא: "In its mother's milk." From this I would know only about its mother's milk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק has a different job, which is explained in a ברייתא. This step only starts the ברייתא, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא opens with a familiar pattern: "I have only..." This means the plain words, read by themselves, cover only a narrow case: the mother's own milk. The ברייתא is getting ready to show how other milk is also included.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (another lesson)
I have only (the narrow case the words state plainly)
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: It is needed for that which is taught in a ברייתא:
"In its mother's milk":
I have derived only the case of its mother's milk;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 23's question by pointing to a ברייתא that uses the פסוק for a different lesson.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the words ״בַּחֲלֵב אִמּוֹ״ teach if they are not needed for the older sister
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They are used in a ברייתא that starts from the narrow case of the mother's milk and then goes on to include more.
